decisions.reason: Define ADLBHY.PARAM enumerates the combined label with bilirubin 1.5 x ULN, while the original SAP page-39 Hy's Law shell labels the combined assessment with bilirubin 2 x ULN. The rendered page confirms a threshold difference rather than a text extraction artifact.

Original SAP page-12 defines the modified combined assessment with bilirubin greater than 1.5*ULN, while its page-39 Hy's Law shell names bilirubin 2 x ULN for the combined assessment. These retained descriptions give different thresholds for the corresponding combined parameter.

Define ADLBHY.STUDYID names ADSL.STUDYID, while adlbhy.yaml reads VINFO.STUDYID from ADLBC. Upstream adlbc.yaml row families take STUDYID from LB rather than ADSL, so this chain does not preserve the documented source.

Dataguide page-4 states the ADSL merge source for STUDYID. The adlbhy.yaml VINFO -> ADLBC path resolves through adlbc.yaml rows to LB.STUDYID, replacing that source despite the copied submission comment.

adlbhy.yaml VINFO.SUBJID reads ADLBC.SUBJID, and upstream adlbc.yaml SUBJID reads ADSL_SBJ.SUBJID from its ADSL input. This transitive copy preserves Define ADLBHY.SUBJID's ADSL.SUBJID source; CR-4 explicitly allows intermediates.

Define ADLBHY.USUBJID names ADSL.USUBJID, while adlbhy.yaml base and derived rows read ADLBC.USUBJID. Upstream adlbc.yaml row families read LB.USUBJID, so inspection of the full chain does not recover the named ADSL source.

Dataguide page-4 names ADSL as the core-variable merge source. The adlbhy.yaml row values resolve through ADLBC to LB.USUBJID, and using the identifier as an ADSL lookup key does not copy its output from ADSL.

SAP page-11 includes laboratory actual-date assignment. adlbhy.yaml copies ADLBC.AVISIT, whose upstream adlbc.yaml ordinary rows map collected LB.VISIT labels and perform no date-window assignment.
SAP page-11 defines randomization-relative visit-window days. Neither adlbhy.yaml nor its adlbc.yaml AVISIT source logic calculates or uses those days for visit assignment.

SAP page-11 requires the closest assessment to each target when a window contains multiple assessments. Neither adlbhy.yaml row grouping nor upstream adlbc.yaml AVISIT branches implement a target-distance selection.

SAP page-11 includes retrieval visits for Week 24 selection. Upstream adlbc.yaml excludes RETRIEVAL before producing the AVISIT values inherited by adlbhy.yaml, and no downstream branch restores that selection.
SAP page-11 requires the preceding assessment when target distances tie. No adlbhy.yaml or upstream adlbc.yaml visit helper expresses that tie rule.

Dataguide page-6 describes records per lab test code per sample per subject. adlbhy.yaml bilihy, transhy and hylaw group only by subject and analysis visit, with no sample identifier or selection to preserve that documented granularity.

Define ADLBHY.PARAM specifies the LBTEST/LBSTRESU concatenation for original tests. adlbhy.yaml base copies ADLBC.PARAM, whose adlbc.yaml _PARAM_BASE helper uses fixed LBTESTCD labels instead of the stated source descriptor fields.

Original Define ADLBHY.AVAL.BILIHY (line 13176) explicitly thresholds R2A1HI, and upstream adlbc.yaml R2A1HI is the unrounded laboratory value divided by its upper limit. With the positive upper limits in the retained source, this expresses the SAP page-12 elevation comparison; the quoted ratio lookup does not establish a different computation.

Original Define ADLBHY.AVAL.TRANSHY (line 13186) explicitly uses either ALT/AST R2A1HI above 1.5. Upstream adlbc.yaml calculates those unrounded value/upper-limit ratios, so the transhy ratio lookup implements SAP page-12's elevation criterion rather than contradicting it.

adlbhy.yaml bilihy/transhy/hylaw create rows whenever any ALT, AST or BILI record exists at the visit. Dataguide page-6 and the native AVAL parameter comments do not state that any-test row-creation condition.

SAP page-11 assigns laboratory assessments to date windows, but its window table has only ADAS-Cog/CIBIC+ and NPI-X bounds and targets, and Define ADLBHY.AVISIT gives only a label and codelist. The adlbhy.r visit list at L48-L54 shows how the reference was filtered, not a documented laboratory window rule.

Define ADLBHY.ADT states LB.LBDTC converted to SAS date and has no ValueListRef providing derived-parameter exceptions. adlbhy.yaml bilihy, transhy and hylaw explicitly set ADT missing, a condition not stated in another retained section.

Define ADLBHY.ADT states only LB.LBDTC converted to SAS date, with no ValueListRef and no stated source sample or date for the visit-level BILIHY/TRANSHY/HYLAW rows. adlbhy.r L165 clearing ADT on derived rows shows the reference computation, which no retained document states.

The retained Define-XML links ADLBHY.PARAMTYP to ValueList.ADLBHY.PARAMTYP, whose ItemDefs set ALT/AST/BILI missing and BILIHY/TRANSHY/HYLAW to DERIVED, a complete rule; the finding itself attributes the gap to the section adapter. adlbhy.r L86, L101 and L129 compute the same assignment.

Define ADLBHY.PARAM states the LBTEST/LBSTRESU concatenation for original tests and the PARAM_ADLBHY codelist enumerates the three Hy's Law labels, so each branch is stated. A sample key is not needed for a per-test label; adlbhy.r L50-L54 copying the ADLBC label only shows how the reference was produced.

Retained ValueList.ADLBHY.PARCAT1 ItemDefs copy ADLBC.PARCAT1 for ALT/AST/BILI and set HYLAW for the derived parameters, and ADLBC.PARCAT1 is hardcoded to CHEM, so the rule is complete outside the adapter sections. adlbhy.r L87, L102 and L128 compute the same constants.

Retained ItemDef ADLBHY.AVAL.HYLAW conditions on param BILHY, a code absent from PARAMCD_ADLBHY, so the combined rule's source does not resolve as written. adlbhy.r L119-L127 computes HYLAW directly from source ratios, which shows the reference computation but does not document the intended source.

adlbhy.yaml bilihy suppresses BASE when the current _AVAL is missing. Original Define ADLBHY.BASE value-level comments select flagged ADLBC.AVAL and SAP page-17 specifies the baseline visit; neither conditions baseline availability on that current value.

adlbhy.yaml transhy suppresses BASE when the current _AVAL is missing. Original Define ADLBHY.BASE value-level comments select flagged ADLBC.AVAL and SAP page-17 specifies the baseline visit; neither conditions baseline availability on that current value.

Retained ItemDefs ADLBHY.BASE.BILIHY/TRANSHY/HYLAW each read ADLBC.AVAL when ADLBC.ABLFL=Y, but ADLBC has no such parameters, so the derived baseline source is unstated. adlbhy.r L138-L145 instead takes the derived rows' own baseline AVAL, a computation no document states.

Retained ValueList.ADLBHY.A1LO ItemDefs copy ADLBC.A1LO for ALT/AST/BILI and set missing for BILIHY/TRANSHY/HYLAW, a complete rule omitted only by the section adapter. adlbhy.r L167 computes the same missing branch.

Retained ValueList.ADLBHY.A1HI ItemDefs copy ADLBC.A1HI for ALT/AST/BILI and set missing for BILIHY/TRANSHY/HYLAW, a complete rule omitted only by the section adapter. adlbhy.r L168 computes the same missing branch.

Retained ValueList.ADLBHY.R2A1LO ItemDefs copy ADLBC.R2A1LO for ALT/AST/BILI and set missing for BILIHY/TRANSHY/HYLAW, a complete rule omitted only by the section adapter. adlbhy.r L169 computes the same missing branch.

Retained ValueList.ADLBHY.SHIFT1 ItemDefs set ALT/AST/BILI missing and give the three BASE/AVAL pairs for the derived parameters; unlisted pairs simply receive no category, so the rule can be probed. adlbhy.r L151-L157 computes that reading, and the SAP page-17/39 table text does not replace it.

Retained ValueList.ADLBHY.SHIFT1N ItemDefs set ALT/AST/BILI missing and give the numeric code for SHIFT1 on the derived parameters, and the SHIFTN codelist supplies the mapping, so the rule is complete. adlbhy.r L158-L162 computes the same codes.

Retained ValueList.ADLBHY.CRIT1 ItemDefs set ALT/AST/BILI missing and BILIHY/TRANSHY/HYLAW to 'R2A1HI > 1.5', which fully states placement and text. adlbhy.r L61-L64 and L173 place the text on the ordinary rows instead, a contradiction of the documented rule rather than a gap in it.

Retained ItemDefs ADLBHY.CRIT1FL.ALT/AST/BILI test R21AHI > 1.5, a variable neither ADLBHY nor ADLBC defines, so the positive branch needs resolution before a literal probe. adlbhy.r L65-L69 uses R2A1HI, which supports that reading but does not document it.
